A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAN: Fourier Analysis Networks. All 21 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures support reliable matching.

before.justification: V3 reports original experiments on periodic functions, symbolic formulas, forecasting, sentiment analysis, image recognition and LLM scaling, plus additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original periodicity and application experiments, including the appendix results on Burgers’ equation, architectural comparisons, depth and normalization.

M1.justification: The FAN layer, its stacked architecture, gated variant and integrations into other architectures remain unchanged. Equations (9)–(11) retain the same procedure; equation-reference corrections do not modify the method.

E1.justification: All explicitly identified datasets and tasks remain. However, the deleted LLM scaling study does not identify its corpus or training objective sufficiently to determine whether its removal eliminates distinct data/task coverage or only different scales of language-model evaluation. Model sizes and token budgets alone do not establish a coverage change.

E2.justification: V3’s scaling study explicitly compares FAN against a standard Transformer using the OLMo architecture; v4 removes that comparison. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including the Fourier-network, FNO, FEDformer and Snake comparisons.

E3.justification: V4 removes the entire scaling evaluation protocol: models with 268M, 604M, 1.0B, 2.6B and 6.7B parameters, and evaluation of a 1.0B model every 20B tokens through 200B tokens. This substantially reduces the experimental design, while the retained experiments’ settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The parameter- and training-token-scaling analysis in v3 Section 3.3 and Figure 7 is deleted, removing a substantial investigation of scalability and efficiency. It is not relocated: the retained appendix analyses of coefficients, periodic-feature width, network depth, normalization and Snake address different questions.

E5.justification: The retained results use unchanged statistical reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, and the deleted scaling study supplies no such uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V4 removes the scaling-loss curves and their quantitative findings, including comparable performance with 69.2% of the Transformer’s parameters and with 159.6B versus 200B training tokens. These are substantial removed results, rather than changed same-setting performance. Numerical results in the retained tables and matched figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14) and the universal-approximation reasoning remain unchanged. Appendix E adds 'sufficiently large' to its existing finite-width explanation, clarifying the theorem statement without introducing a substantively different theorem, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the explicit claim that FAN exhibits a steeper scaling-law curve than standard Transformer as model size and training tokens increase. The abstract and central claims about general-purpose periodicity modeling, architectural substitution and benchmark effectiveness remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Deleting the scaling paragraph removes its interpretation that FAN offers greater parameter and training-data efficiency at LLM scale. The broader mechanism and generalization discussion remains, including a learning-efficiency argument whose supporting reference becomes 'Figure ??'. Future work also specifies theoretical foundations for tasks such as language modeling.

D1.justification: Appendix C.6 removes the disclosure that the CNN baseline was generated by ChatGPT, while retaining its architecture and training settings. The deleted scaling study also loses its OLMo implementation reference. Hardware, other implementation details and the code-access disclosure remain unchanged; no CNN implementation change is established.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds works on complex-valued networks, oscillatory Fourier networks, NeRF, N-BEATS and Fourier features, and removes the OLMo and Kaplan scaling-law references. The related-work discussion itself remains essentially unchanged, so this is a limited reference-list revision rather than substantial repositioning.

P1.justification: V4 introduces a separate '4 Experiments' heading, renumbers subsequent sections and repairs malformed equation references. Small wording changes appear in Appendix E and future work. The retained prose is largely unchanged, without extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: V3’s two-panel scaling Figure 7 is removed. Figure 6 moves from page 8 to page 9, Table 6 moves from page 10 to page 9, and subsequent figures are renumbered. Other displays retain their content and design, with accompanying page reflow.

improvement.justification: V4 improves section organization and removes the explicit scaling-law claim alongside its experiment. However, deleting v3 Figure 7 removes direct evidence for scalability while retaining the foundation-model motivation and learning-efficiency discussion; the latter now contains 'Figure ??'. The resulting loss of support and internal coherence outweighs the limited editorial gains, while the unchanged method and extensive retained experiments keep the deterioration limited.
